title: Skills vs Tools vs Use Cases
tagline: Three words IronClaw users mix up
outro: Skills teach. Tools act. Use cases deliver.
script: Skills, tools, use cases — IronClaw users mix these up constantly. Here's the difference in sixty seconds. A tool is something your agent can do: send a Slack message, open a pull request, read a spreadsheet. Tools run sandboxed, and every call passes through a security boundary. A skill is something your agent knows: a playbook, written in plain Markdown, that teaches it how to handle a job — your release process, your report format, your rules. And a use case? That's what you actually wanted: a morning briefing, a portfolio monitor, a Telegram assistant. Use cases are just skills and tools composed together. Teach it with skills. Equip it with tools. Ship the use case.
